name: Feedback Loop (Feature 7)
description: Allow users to rate findings and use feedback to adjust system behavior. Record findings with feedback_ids. Add 'stigmergy feedback <id> [helpful|already_knew|wrong|irrelevant]' CLI command. Store feedback in .stigmergy/feedback.jsonl. Initially adjust only agent confidence scores via attention/calibration.py (calibration_lr_up/down). 'already_knew' = mild positive (correct but low novelty, slightly decrease surfacing priority). Three sub-components: feedback_recording (storage and record management), feedback_cli (CLI command interface), feedback_calibration (rating-to-calibration mapping and application). Shared types module provides Rating StrEnum, CalibrationDimension StrEnum, frozen Pydantic record models, and unified error hierarchy. ID convention: fnd-{timestamp_hex}-{random_hex} for findings, fbk-{timestamp_hex}-{random_hex} for feedback records. CalibratorProtocol enables dependency inversion for testability. ENABLED_DIMENSIONS gate controls which calibration dimensions are active; initially only agent_confidence.

types.name: Rating
types.description: StrEnum of the four possible user feedback ratings for a finding. Shared across all sub-components. Implemented as StrEnum in Python so each variant serializes to its lowercase string value. Rating input from CLI is normalized to lowercase before matching.

types.name: CalibrationDimension
types.description: The calibration dimension a CalibrationAction targets. Enables dual-signal nature of 'already_knew' (accuracy + novelty). Only 'agent_confidence' is initially enabled via ENABLED_DIMENSIONS gate; others are deferred until Features 3 and 4 land.

types.name: FeedbackStatus
types.description: Outcome status of applying feedback through the calibration pipeline. 'applied' = all actions applied, 'partial' = some skipped due to disabled dimensions, 'skipped' = all actions skipped.

types.name: CLIExitCode
types.description: Exit codes used by the CLI layer when handling feedback commands. Maps error types to numeric exit codes for scripting/automation compatibility. 0=success, 1=id_not_found, 2=invalid_rating, 3=io_error, 4=unexpected.

types.name: FeedbackCalibrationConfig

fields.name: helpful_confidence_delta
fields.description: Positive delta applied to agent_confidence when rating is 'helpful'. Corresponds to calibration_lr_up.

fields.name: wrong_confidence_delta
fields.description: Negative delta magnitude applied to agent_confidence when rating is 'wrong'. Corresponds to calibration_lr_down. Must be > irrelevant_confidence_delta.

fields.name: irrelevant_confidence_delta
fields.description: Negative delta magnitude (smaller than 'wrong') applied to agent_confidence when rating is 'irrelevant'. Corresponds to calibration_lr_down.

fields.description: Mild positive delta applied to agent_confidence when rating is 'already_knew' (correct but low novelty). Effectively helpful_confidence_delta * 0.25 by default. Corresponds to calibration_lr_up.

fields.description: Negative delta magnitude applied to surfacing_priority when rating is 'already_knew' (slightly decrease surfacing priority for low-novelty correct findings). Effectively wrong_confidence_delta * 0.5 by default. Corresponds to calibration_lr_down. Deferred until surfacing_priority is enabled.

functions.name: FeedbackStore.load
functions.description: Async method to load existing findings and feedback records from JSONL files into in-memory indexes. Reads findings.jsonl and feedback.jsonl from configured paths. Each JSONL line has a 'record_type' discriminator ('finding' or 'feedback'). Defensive parsing: blank lines and malformed JSON lines are skipped with a warning logged. If files do not exist, indexes remain empty (no error). For feedback records, latest entry per feedback_id wins (append-only re-rating). Uses asyncio.to_thread for file I/O.

functions.name: map_rating_to_actions
functions.description: Pure synchronous function. Maps a Rating to a complete list of CalibrationActions across ALL dimensions (including deferred ones). Uses exhaustive match with assert_never to guarantee all rating variants are handled. The returned actions represent the full intent; filtering by enabled dimensions happens separately in filter_enabled_actions. Rating→action mapping: 'helpful' → [(agent_confidence, +helpful_confidence_delta)], 'wrong' → [(agent_confidence, -wrong_confidence_delta)], 'irrelevant' → [(agent_confidence, -irrelevant_confidence_delta)], 'already_knew' → [(agent_confidence, +already_knew_confidence_delta), (surfacing_priority, -already_knew_surfacing_priority_delta)].

inputs.name: rating
inputs.description: The user's feedback rating.

inputs.name: config
inputs.description: Configuration providing delta magnitudes for each rating→dimension pair.

error_cases.name: invalid_rating
error_cases.condition: rating value is not a valid Rating variant (should be impossible with proper typing; assert_never catches at runtime)

preconditions: rating is a valid Rating variant
config contains valid positive magnitude values for all delta fields
postconditions: Returned list is non-empty (every rating produces at least one action)
Each action has a non-empty description
Each action's delta is in [-1.0, 1.0]
For 'helpful': exactly 1 action with dimension='agent_confidence' and delta > 0 equal to +config.helpful_confidence_delta
For 'wrong': exactly 1 action with dimension='agent_confidence' and delta < 0 equal to -config.wrong_confidence_delta
For 'irrelevant': exactly 1 action with dimension='agent_confidence' and delta < 0 equal to -config.irrelevant_confidence_delta
For 'already_knew': exactly 2 actions — (agent_confidence, +config.already_knew_confidence_delta) and (surfacing_priority, -config.already_knew_surfacing_priority_delta)
All Rating variants are exhaustively handled (assert_never guarantees this at type-check time)

functions.name: filter_enabled_actions
functions.description: Pure synchronous function. Partitions a list of CalibrationActions into (enabled, skipped) based on the ENABLED_DIMENSIONS gate from config. Actions whose dimension is in enabled_dimensions are placed in the enabled list; all others go to skipped. Skipped actions represent deferred feature dimensions.

inputs.name: actions
inputs.description: List of CalibrationActions to partition.

inputs.name: config
inputs.description: Configuration providing the list of enabled dimensions.

preconditions: actions is a valid list of CalibrationAction (may be empty)
postconditions: len(enabled) + len(skipped) == len(actions) — all input actions are accounted for
Every action in enabled has dimension in config.enabled_dimensions
Every action in skipped has dimension NOT in config.enabled_dimensions
Order of actions is preserved within each partition

functions.name: apply_feedback
functions.description: Async function. Processes a single FeedbackEntry: maps rating to actions via map_rating_to_actions, filters by enabled dimensions via filter_enabled_actions, applies enabled actions via the CalibratorProtocol (positive delta → calibration_lr_up, negative delta → calibration_lr_down with abs(delta)), and returns a FeedbackResult. Skipped actions (deferred dimensions) are logged at DEBUG level and included in FeedbackResult.skipped_actions.

inputs.name: entry
inputs.description: The feedback entry to process.

inputs.name: calibrator
inputs.description: An object implementing CalibratorProtocol (has async calibration_lr_up and calibration_lr_down methods). Typed as CalibratorProtocol at runtime.

inputs.name: config
inputs.description: Calibration configuration with delta magnitudes and enabled dimensions.

result.status is 'skipped' if all actions were skipped (no enabled dimensions matched)
len(result.applied_actions) + len(result.skipped_actions) == total actions from map_rating_to_actions
calibrator.calibration_lr_up was called once for each applied action with delta > 0
calibrator.calibration_lr_down was called once for each applied action with delta < 0 (with abs(delta))

functions.name: process_feedback_batch
functions.description: Async function. Processes a sequence of FeedbackEntry items sequentially (to preserve ordering semantics of feedback), applying each via apply_feedback. Collects and returns all FeedbackResults. If an individual entry fails, its error is captured in the result (status='skipped', reason=error message) and processing continues with the next entry — batch processing is fail-safe.

inputs.description: List of FeedbackEntry items to process. May be empty.

inputs.name: calibrator
inputs.description: An object implementing CalibratorProtocol.

inputs.name: config
inputs.description: Calibration configuration.

preconditions: entries is a valid sequence of FeedbackEntry (may be empty)
calibrator implements CalibratorProtocol
postconditions: len(results) == len(entries) — one result per input entry
results[i].feedback_id == entries[i].feedback_id for all i
Entries are processed sequentially in input order
A failure on entry[i] does not prevent processing of entry[i+1]
If entries is empty, returns an empty list
Failed entries have status='skipped' and reason containing the error message
side_effects: Calls calibrator methods for each entry's enabled actions
Logs each entry's processing outcome at INFO level
Logs individual failures at WARNING level

invariants: Every finding feedback_id starts with prefix 'fnd-' followed by {timestamp_hex}-{random_hex}; every feedback record_id starts with prefix 'fbk-'
FindingRecord, FeedbackRecord, FeedbackEntry, CalibrationAction, FeedbackResult, FeedbackCalibrationConfig, and FeedbackStoreConfig are all frozen (immutable) once created
FeedbackRecord is a denormalized superset of FindingRecord fields plus rating, feedback_timestamp, and record_id
The in-memory index is always consistent with the on-disk JSONL files after successful writes
A FeedbackRecord can only exist for a feedback_id that has a corresponding FindingRecord
Re-rating a finding appends a new FeedbackRecord line; get_feedback returns the latest rating for a given feedback_id
Write operations on FeedbackStore are serialized via asyncio.Lock (single-process concurrency model)
Blank and malformed JSONL lines are skipped with a warning during file reads — never cause crashes
Each JSONL line has a 'record_type' discriminator ('finding' or 'feedback') to distinguish record types
schema_version field on records enables future migration of stored records
content_summary is limited to 500 characters maximum
All file I/O is performed via asyncio.to_thread to avoid blocking the event loop
Directory .stigmergy/ is auto-created on first write if it does not exist
Rating input from CLI is matched case-insensitively (normalized to lowercase before comparison)
CLI exit codes: 0=success, 1=id_not_found, 2=invalid_rating, 3=io_error, 4=unexpected
The CLI layer contains no business logic; all validation and persistence logic resides in domain functions
FeedbackError is the base exception type; FeedbackNotFoundError, DuplicateFeedbackError, InvalidFeedbackRatingError, CalibrationApplicationError, FeedbackIOError, FeedbackParseError are subtypes
ENABLED_DIMENSIONS is initially frozenset({'agent_confidence'}); only dimensions in this set are applied, all others are skipped and logged
map_rating_to_actions uses exhaustive match with assert_never — adding a new Rating variant without updating the match is a type error
Feedback processing order is preserved: batch entries are processed sequentially in input order for temporal consistency
All delta magnitudes in FeedbackCalibrationConfig are positive; the sign (up/down) is determined by map_rating_to_actions based on rating semantics
CalibratorProtocol uses structural subtyping (typing.Protocol) — no inheritance from a base class is required
A 'helpful' rating always results in calibration_lr_up on agent_confidence with delta = +helpful_confidence_delta
A 'wrong' rating always results in calibration_lr_down on agent_confidence with delta = -wrong_confidence_delta (largest negative magnitude)
An 'irrelevant' rating always results in calibration_lr_down on agent_confidence with delta = -irrelevant_confidence_delta (smaller than wrong)

An 'already_knew' rating results in a mild calibration_lr_up on agent_confidence (+already_knew_confidence_delta) AND a deferred calibration_lr_down on surfacing_priority (-already_knew_surfacing_priority_delta)
wrong_confidence_delta > irrelevant_confidence_delta (wrong is penalized more heavily than irrelevant)
Deferred dimensions (surfacing_priority, business_weight, familiarity_weight) are computed in map_rating_to_actions but filtered out by filter_enabled_actions until corresponding features enable them
All public functions have type annotations and docstrings
All models are frozen Pydantic v2 BaseModels with model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)
Tests mock the CalibratorProtocol and use tmp_path for JSONL files
